history: Economico is a trap for many learners. In Italian it means both ‘economic’ and ‘cheap’: un albergo economico is an inexpensive hotel, and un biglietto economico a low-priced ticket. The word comes from Greek oikonomía, ‘management of a household’, built from oikos, ‘house’, and nemein, ‘to manage, to distribute’. Economy was originally housekeeping: how a family or an estate spends and saves. A person who managed the household well did not waste money, so the adjective took on the meaning of ‘saving, low-cost’. Later the idea grew from the house to the state, and l'economia is the whole system of production and trade. Notice also the relative ecologia, which shares the first part, oikos.
historyEinfach: Economico comes from Greek oikos, ‘house’, and nemein, ‘to manage’. Economy was first the management of a household. In Italian, economico means ‘economic’ and also ‘cheap, not expensive’: un ristorante economico is a cheap restaurant. The word ecologia has the same first part, oikos.
